claims.text: Inducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys can preserve structural integrity.
Inducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations will improve the heat-transfer capability of tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The initial material is a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy produced by conventional solidification or laser cladding.
Conventionally processed tungsten refractory HEAs have a baseline microstructure containing incoherent or randomly distributed precipitates.
A tailored post-solidification heat treatment with controlled multistep cooling will form uniformly distributed coherent nanoprecipitates.
Temperatures of 800–1200 °C are representative of elevated plasma-facing reactor operating conditions for the proposed alloy.
The proposed benefit will hold under high heat flux and cyclic thermal-mechanical loading.
SCCPs provide coherent, well-defined interfaces in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces reduce interfacial thermal resistance.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces minimize phonon scattering.
Coherent interfaces act as low-resistance channels for electron and phonon transport.
Improved electron and phonon transport through coherent interfaces enhances thermal conductivity.
SCCP coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that can cause premature cracking.
The SCCP-reinforced microstructure will withstand irradiation.
The treated alloy will have more than 10% higher effective thermal conductivity than the baseline alloy.
SCCP treatment will avoid degradation, and may slightly improve, hardness and tensile strength.
SCCP-strengthened tungsten refractory HEAs can retain high yield strength at 800 °C.
The performance improvement will persist during prolonged exposure to simulated plasma-facing conditions and cyclic thermal loads.
The exact magnitude of the conductivity improvement and the long-term irradiation stability of SCCPs remain uncertain.
A conductivity increase below 10%, lack of statistical significance, or degradation of mechanical properties after cycling would falsify the hypothesis.
